title: Square roots and irrational numbers
lede: Undoing a square, estimating roots in your head, and the numbers that never end.

sections.md:
## Square roots
The **square root** of a number is what you square to get it. √49 = 7 because 7² = 49.

Perfect squares to know cold: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81, 100, 121, 144, 169, 196, 225.

## Estimating
To estimate √50, find the perfect squares around it: 49 < 50 < 64, so √50 is between 7 and 8, very close to 7 (since 50 is right next to 49). √50 ≈ 7.07.

## Rational vs irrational
- **Rational** numbers can be written as a fraction of integers: 3, −2/5, 0.75, 0.333… (= 1/3). Their decimals either stop or repeat.
- **Irrational** numbers can't. Their decimals go on forever with no repeating pattern: √2 = 1.41421356…, π = 3.14159265…

The square root of any whole number that isn't a perfect square is irrational.

## Cube roots
∛27 = 3 because 3³ = 27. Unlike square roots, cube roots of negatives work: ∛(−8) = −2.
